Joy Harrell-Goff elected Chair; Xavier Cason elected Vice Chair.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Special Called Meeting | 7/21/26
conflicts.issue: Timing and Approval of 2026-27 Salary Scales
conflicts.summary: Board debated whether to immediately approve the 2026-27 salary scales to ensure timely payroll processing for July or refer them entirely to the August Finance Committee for further study.
conflicts.side_a_position: Immediate approval of salary scales to ensure payroll processing without retropay delays
side_a_arguments: Staff need pay scales adopted immediately for July paychecks without waiting or risking employee delays/retropay issues
District should not delay low-income classified staff raises
conflicts.side_b_position: Referral of salary scales to Finance Committee before final board vote
side_b_arguments: Desire for further study in Finance Committee before voting, ensuring comprehensive review of arithmetic and classified schedules
conflicts.resolution: Approved 4-3 as amended, with minimum wage and related details referred to the August 19 Finance Committee meeting.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 11/19/26
conflicts.issue: Debate over the MGT consulting contract, school rightsizing studies, facility utilization, and how to prepare capital needs and enrollment projections for the county bond proposal.
conflicts.summary: Debate between board members and administration over the MGT consulting contract and how to conduct school rightsizing and capital needs analyses.
conflicts.side_a_position: Opposed to the MGT contract and seeking alternative/revised directive approaches.
side_a_arguments: Support for community-driven planning, questioning the cost and necessity of the MGT contract, and emphasizing comprehensive community engagement and local demographers.
conflicts.side_b_position: Supported comprehensive planning and administrative recommendations for facility studies.
side_b_arguments: Emphasized that the comprehensive rightsizing study is necessary to analyze enrollment projections and facility needs objectively for the county commissioners and bond advocacy.
conflicts.resolution: Board voted 5-2 to order administration not to take action on the MGT contract, and subsequently voted 2-5 against a directive motion regarding a capital needs status report.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 8/13/26
conflicts.issue: Discussion regarding process and rushing of the unlimited instructor contract for EC teacher vacancies
conflicts.summary: Debate over whether to approve the third-party unlimited instructor contract for EC vacancies given the short notice and procedural bypass versus the urgent student need.
conflicts.side_a_position: Expressing concern over process and rushing without adequate public notice
side_a_arguments: Board members raised concerns about the short notice (contract received late day before) and bypassing standard committee review/public notice process
side_a_members: Wendell Tabb (noted a no vote on process/procedure)
conflicts.side_b_position: Putting student needs first and acting urgently despite procedural friction
side_b_arguments: There is an urgent need to fill 28 Exceptional Children (EC) teacher vacancies in the district to support students
conflicts.resolution: Approved unanimously after debate on process and urgency

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Special Called Meeting | 7/21/26
conflicts.issue: Lions Farm Elementary Overcrowding & Modular Classroom Expansion
conflicts.summary: Board members discussed whether approving modular classrooms at Lions Farm Elementary conflicted with district-wide right-sizing goals or lacked sufficient community engagement.
conflicts.side_a_position: Immediate approval of modular expansion to address severe overcrowding and safety violations
side_a_arguments: School is severely overcrowded (100+ over capacity), classrooms under stairwells violate fire codes, and 12-15 month lead time requires immediate action for 2027-28
conflicts.side_b_position: Delay or more extensive community engagement and alignment with district right-sizing before committing to modular expansion
side_b_arguments: Concerns regarding community engagement, equity of capital investments across the district, and alignment with the broader right-sizing RFP
conflicts.resolution: Approved unanimously with referral of boundary discussions to the Facilities Committee.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 11/5/26
conflicts.issue: Proposed consulting services contract with MGT Impact Solutions for a district-wide right-sizing and consolidation study
conflicts.summary: Board members debated whether to approve a consulting services contract with MGT Impact Solutions for a right-sizing and school consolidation study, with some raising concerns over the firm's background and community impact while administration and others emphasized proactive fiscal planning for aging facilities and upcoming bond requirements.
conflicts.side_a_position: Support approving the MGT consulting contract to study right-sizing and facility consolidation options.
side_a_arguments: Proactive fiscal stewardship is required to evaluate aging facilities (average age 65 years), manage capital improvement needs ($965M in deferred maintenance), and prepare justifications for the upcoming 2028 bond referendum under state/county expectations.
conflicts.side_b_position: Expressed hesitation and opposition to awarding the contract to MGT Impact Solutions without re-evaluating options or decoupling right-sizing.
side_b_arguments: Concerns regarding the consulting firm's background with school closures and privatization, potential community anxiety over school closures, and preference to explore other consultants or remove consolidation from the study.
conflicts.resolution: Discussed at length during the work session without a formal vote taken on the contract itself (moved to future action/consent).

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 11/19/26
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education held its monthly meeting on November 19, 2026, featuring celebrations for students, educators, and the DPS Principal of the Year, alongside updates on advanced academics. The board engaged in extensive discussions on facility planning, capital needs, and school rightsizing. Formal votes were taken on the agenda, meeting minutes, an instruction for administration not to take action on the MGT consulting contract (passed 5-2), a subsequent capital needs directive motion (failed 2-5), budget amendment number two, and entering closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Opening Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board President called the monthly meeting to order, welcomed attendees and interpreters, introduced student representatives, and held a moment of silence.

agenda_items.title: Recognitions and Celebrations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board celebrated outstanding students, teachers, and staff members, including the Student of the Month Denine Omar, Teacher of the Month Julia Champion, Employee of the Month Karen Jones, and Principal of the Year Dr. Tawana Stewart.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Lewis provided an update on district progress, celebrating National Career Development Month, School Psychology Week, Homelessness Awareness Month, winter sports media day, the Showcase of Schools, and the Durham Early College of Health Sciences documentary premiere.

agenda_items.title: Advanced Academics Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented advanced academics data highlighting district growth in AP participation and performance, IB programs, AIG identification, and credit by demonstrated mastery (CDM).

agenda_items.title: Discussion on MGT Contract, Facility Utilization, and Bond Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board engaged in an extensive debate regarding the MGT consulting contract, facility utilization, school rightsizing studies, and capital needs preparation for the upcoming county bond proposal.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Order administration not to take any action with the MGT contract passed 5-2; directive motion for comprehensive status report failed 2-5

agenda_items.title: Budget Resolution and Amendment Number One Technical Correction
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a technical correction and alignment of budget resolution and amendment number one to match the local county budget ordinance formatting.

agenda_items.title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted to move into closed session to preserve attorney-client privilege regarding a specific Industrial Commission case.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Budget Amendment Number Two
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented Budget Amendment Number Two, covering state hospital school positions, capital outlay carryover projects, federal indirect cost revenue adjustments, and minor grant budgets.

votes.item_title: Approval of Agenda
votes.discussion_detail: The board convened its monthly meeting with the call to order by the Chair, followed by a welcome to attendees, introduction of student representatives such as Superintendent Student Advisory Council member Kristen Nivea, a moment of silence, and an opening overview of November celebrations by Ms. Cooper recognizing students, teachers, employees, and the Principal of the Year. Ms. Rivero moved to approve the agenda, seconded by Ms. Burr. The motion passed unanimously with no recorded nays.

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes (September 24, 2026)
votes.discussion_detail: The board considered the approval of the meeting minutes from September 24, 2026, as part of the opening proceedings following the call to order and opening celebrations. Ms. Rivero moved to approve the minutes, and Mr. Cason seconded the motion. The minutes were approved unanimously by the board with no dissenting votes.

votes.item_title: Order administration not to take any action with the MGT contract
votes.discussion_detail: The board discussed administrative actions regarding the MGT contract following extensive deliberation on enrollment trends, facility conditions, utilization studies, and robust enrollment initiatives. Following discussion on direction for the administration, a vote was taken to order administration not to take any action with the MGT contract. The motion was moved by Ms. Rogers and seconded by Ms. Rivero. The motion passed by a 5-2 vote after board members discussed the clear direction for administration moving forward.

votes.item_title: Directive motion for comprehensive status report on capital needs and bond proposal
votes.discussion_detail: Ms. Rivero moved to direct administration to create a comprehensive status report on Durham Public Schools capital needs and submission for Durham County to create a bond proposal that includes updated enrollment projections for the next 10 years, analysis of facility conditions and utilization, and a needs assessment for under-enrolled schools; the motion was seconded by Ms. Ben-Kateb. During discussion, board members debated the implications of the directive, timing, and relationship to previous phases and cost guardrails raised by staff such as Mr. Barnes regarding RFPs and community engagement. Mr. Cason indicated his intent to vote the motion down to allow alternative facility discussions, and the motion ultimately failed on a 2-5 vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of Budget Amendment Number Two
votes.discussion_detail: The board considered Approval of Budget Amendment Number Two, which involved completing the budgeting of indirect cost revenue now that all federal grants have been settled with the federal fiscal year starting in October, along with small minor grants totaling around $8,400. Ms. Rogers moved to approve the budget amendment, seconded by Ms. Rivero. The motion passed unanimously with no opposition. Subsequently, the board also unanimously approved budget resolution and technical amendment number one to align formatting with the county budget ordinance with additional local fund details.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.discussion_detail: A motion was made by Ms. Rogers and seconded by Mr. Cason to enter into closed session for the reasons stated in the agenda and to preserve attorney-client privilege in order to discuss the legal matter of Thomas Gione versus Durham Public Schools Industrial Commission, specifically referencing file number 257457371 (noted during discussion). Prior to this motion, the board discussed budget amendments, local fund details formatting, and community engagement strategies related to moving bond projects forward. There was no further discussion on the closed session motion itself when called, and the motion passed unanimously with all members voting in favor.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 11/5/26
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education held its monthly work session on November 5, 2026, featuring presentations from Durham County Sheriff Birkhead on the SRO program and Dr. Jennifer Hall on school improvement plans and low-performing school exits. The board engaged in an extensive policy debate regarding a proposed consulting services contract with MGT Impact Solutions for a district-wide right-sizing and consolidation study. Additionally, the board approved procedural agenda amendments, approved meeting minutes, adopted a proclamation recognizing National Homeless Children and Youth Awareness Month, and discussed upcoming NCSBA legislative agenda priorities and student engagement initiatives.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members discussed amendments to the agenda, moving item O off consent to a new operations section and bringing item 3A forward, as well as adding the NCSBA legislative agenda item.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 6-0-0 (Multiple motions to amend and approve agenda)

agenda_items.title: Sheriff's Office SRO Program Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County Sheriff Birkhead presented an update on the School Resource Officer (SRO) program, highlighting positive trends in juvenile petitions, restorative justice circles, and positive student relationships.

agenda_items.title: Approval of October 8, 2026 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved the work session minutes from October 8, 2026.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community members spoke during public comment on various district topics including educational equity, resources, and student support.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation for National Homeless Children and Youth Awareness Month (November 2026)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board read and approved a proclamation recognizing November 2026 as National Homeless Children and Youth Awareness Month, discussing McKinney-Vento support and student housing insecurity.

agenda_items.title: School Improvement Plans & Low-Performing Schools Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Jennifer Hall presented an update on school improvement plans and low-performing school designations, noting 16 low-performing schools and successful exits for six schools.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Consulting Services Contract with MGT Impact Solutions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Extensive board deliberation and administration presentation regarding the proposed consulting services contract with MGT Impact Solutions for a district-wide right-sizing and consolidation study.
agenda_items.vote_summary: No formal vote (extended deliberation; contract revisions requested for Nov 19 meeting)

agenda_items.title: Student Voice & Belonging Initiative Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members discussed student voice initiatives, belonging, and engagement strategies across district schools.

agenda_items.title: NCSBA Legislative Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members reviewed the NCSBA legislative agenda, discussing positions on school safety grants, teacher pay decompression, and state funding.

votes.item_title: Agenda Amendment (Moving item off consent and adding operations section)
votes.discussion_detail: Ms. Burr moved to amend the agenda by moving item O off the consent agenda and creating a new Operations section as item A after academic services. When asked by another member to explain the reason for moving the item, Ms. Burr stated that they received numerous emails today and believed members of the public were present to discuss the item publicly. The motion was seconded by Ms. Rivero and approved unanimously in a 6-0-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Agenda Amendment (Moving item 3A and adding NCSBA legislative agenda item)
votes.discussion_detail: Millicent Rogers moved to amend the agenda by moving item 3A to occur immediately as the next item before general public comment and minutes, and to add an agenda item under Board of Education (item B) for the board to review the NCSBA legislative priority document. The motion was seconded by Ms. Rivero and approved unanimously by a 6-0-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of Agenda as Amended
votes.discussion_detail: Following prior amendments, Ms. Rivero moved to approve the overall agenda as amended, which was seconded by Ms. Ben Kateb. The motion passed unanimously in a 6-0-0 vote without opposition, allowing the board to proceed with the scheduled presentations and time-sensitive guest remarks.

votes.item_title: Approval of October 8, 2026 Work Session Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Ms. Burr moved to approve the work session minutes dated October 8, 2026, with a second from Ms. Rivero. The motion passed 5-0-0 as Millicent Rogers arrived right at the conclusion of the vote.

votes.item_title: Proclamation for National Homeless Children and Youth Awareness Month (November 2026)
votes.discussion_detail: Following a presentation by Tumika Wor Satterfield, Director of Student Wellness and Advocacy, on McKinney-Vento programming and student support, Millicent Rogers moved to approve the proclamation declaring November 2026 as National Homeless Children and Youth Awareness Month. The motion was seconded by Ms. Kataev and approved unanimously in a 6-0-0 vote. Following the vote, board members engaged in a discussion regarding housing insecurity numbers in Durham Public Schools and strategies to address student homelessness.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 10/8/26
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education held its monthly work session on October 8, 2026. The board discussed and approved agenda amendments—including referring the districtwide right-sizing and consolidation study contract back to the facilities committee and adding a presentation from the UNCC School of Government. They also heard updates on transportation and school safety, approved proclamations for National Bullying Prevention Month and Disability History and Awareness Month, and received informational presentations on Cognia accreditation and school improvement plans.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Moment of Silence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board chair called the meeting to order, welcomed student representatives, and led a moment of silence for a fallen Durham firefighter and in observance of NCCU homecoming.

agenda_items.title: Monthly Celebrations and Recognitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: District leaders and school principals recognized outstanding students of the month (Phineas PoDexter and Aaron Pritchard) and educators/employees of the month (Margaret Radic and Juan Guerrero) with certificates and community partner awards.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed and amended the meeting agenda, voting unanimously to remove item P (right-sizing study) for committee review, add the UNCC School of Government presentation as item 3A, move overnight international field trips to information only, and approve the agenda as amended.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved the minutes from the previous board work session held on September 10, 2026.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Approved work session minutes from September 10, 2026 (Passed, 7-0)

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community members spoke during public comment on various district matters, including policies, school resources, and student support.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approvals
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed the consent agenda and approved routine administrative and financial items.

agenda_items.title: UNCC School of Government Property Study Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Representatives from the UNCC School of Government presented findings regarding district-owned properties including old Lowe's Grove, old Northern High School, and the DSA campus.

agenda_items.title: Transportation Department Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation officials provided an update on bus route efficiency, express stop pilot results at DSA, electric bus fleets, and plans for expanding express stops to comprehensive innovative high schools.

agenda_items.title: Safety and Security Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The executive director of safety and security presented an update on emergency response plans (SER), safety compliance, drills, and school safety protocols.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations for National Bullying Prevention Month and Disability History and Awareness Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved proclamations recognizing National Bullying Prevention Month and Disability History and Awareness Month.

agenda_items.title: Cognia District Accreditation Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: District staff presented an overview of Cognia district accreditation standards, cycles, and continuous improvement goals for Durham Public Schools.

agenda_items.title: Strategic Planning and Program Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented early planning and operational frameworks for upcoming district programs and initiatives.

agenda_items.title: Board Policy 6420 Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed board policy 6420 (Contracts with the Board), discussed legal references and local budget transparency requirements, and voted to approve the policy on first read while waiving the second read.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Approved policy 6420 on first read and waived second read (Passed, 7-0)

votes.item_title: Remove item P (districtwide right-sizing and consolidation study) from agenda and refer to facilities committee
votes.discussion_detail: Board member Millicent Rogers moved to remove item P (the districtwide right-sizing and consolidation study) from the agenda and refer it to the facilities committee. Rogers acknowledged that while the board authorized the RFP in June 2026 and administration carried out the work as directed, exercising due diligence on facilities is necessary given limited resources and changing enrollment. The motion was seconded by Gabby Rivero and passed unanimously (7-0).

votes.item_title: Add UNCC School of Government presentation as item 3A
votes.notes: Passed unanimously after procedural discussion regarding notice
votes.discussion_detail: Xavier Cason moved to amend the evening's agenda under item 3 (operations) to add a presentation from the UNCC School of Government, coming from the facilities committee, which was seconded by Chair Joy Harrell-Goff. The presentation covers studies on several DPS-owned properties, including the old Lowe's Grove building, the old Northern High School, and the DSA campus. Despite some initial questions regarding context and timing from board members, the motion passed unanimously (7-0).

votes.item_title: Move overnight international field trips (item 4A) to information only
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Joy Harrell-Goff moved to change item 4A on academic services regarding overnight international field trips from discussion to information only due to the length of the agenda. Following a clarification question from Mr. Tabb regarding administration's reasoning—to which Dr. King responded that it was simply misplaced—the motion was seconded by Nadeen Bir and passed unanimously (7-0).

votes.item_title: Approve agenda as amended
votes.discussion_detail: Millicent Rogers moved to approve the meeting agenda as amended, which was seconded by Gabby Rivero and Wendell Tabb. The motion incorporated prior agenda adjustments regarding committee referrals, the UNCC School of Government presentation, and shifting overnight international field trips to information only. The motion passed unanimously (7-0).

votes.item_title: Approve board work session minutes from September 10, 2026
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Joy Harrell-Goff moved to approve the board work session minutes dated September 10, 2026, which was seconded by Xavier Cason. Following a brief call for discussion and no objections, the motion passed unanimously (7-0).

votes.item_title: Approve National Bullying Prevention Month and Disability History and Awareness Month proclamations
votes.discussion_detail: The board considered and approved both the National Bullying Prevention Month and Disability History and Awareness Month proclamations during the monthly work session. Staff members including counseling coordinator Dr. Sherice Artis and director Tamika Wilson-Satterfield presented the bullying prevention proclamation, highlighting ongoing district efforts. Following the presentation and discussion, Millicent Rogers moved to approve both proclamations, seconded by Chair Joy Harrell-Goff. The motion passed unanimously in a 7-0 vote without dissent or further debate.

meetings.title: Live SeptembeLive September 24#DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 9/24/26
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education held its monthly meeting on September 24, 2026. The board recognized student and employees of the month, received administrative updates on facilities, transportation, and safety, and discussed state bonuses and teacher supplements. Formal votes were taken and passed unanimously to approve: (1) the bonus plan for transportation and monthly employees contingent upon budget amendment one, (2) the state teacher supplement framework including Pre-K and exceptional children's teachers, (3) a resolution opposing the 2026 state constitutional amendments on income and property tax caps, (4) the appointment of 22 applicants to the 2026 legislative steering committee, (5) moving the October board meeting date, (6) policy 3510 (religious-based exemptions from school programs) on second reading, (7) the policy prioritization and tiering recommendations as amended, and (8) moving into closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Welcome, and September Recognitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The meeting opens with the call to order, moment of silence, and agenda review. Following this, DPS holds its September celebrations, honoring Riverside High School student of the month Zooladi Oweno, Glenn Elementary teacher of the month Caitlyn Craig, and Glenn Middle employee of the month Janetta Footman Middleton.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis delivers his superintendent report, covering Hispanic Heritage Month, Suicide Prevention Awareness Month, gun safety and secure storage ('Be SMART'), National Attendance Awareness Month, NC College Connect for seniors, Principal of the Year semi-finalists, Education Policy Fellowship participants, Laura Governor School board appointment, performance data, and the State of the District address.

agenda_items.title: Bonus Plan Approval (October 9 & October 30)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mr. Teter presents the state bonus framework detailing state-funded bonuses for classified and certified staff, along with local funding allocations for custodians and child nutrition staff. Board members discuss the funding mechanics and timing.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 7-0 (Moved by Millicent Rogers, seconded by Mr. Kase)

agenda_items.title: State Teacher Supplement Framework
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mr. Teter presents the state teacher supplement framework, noting that Durham is newly included in state low-wealth/supplement funds ($792 per teacher), and administration recommends using prek funds to include prek and EC prek teachers.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 7-0 (Moved by Miss Burr, seconded by Millicent Rogers)

agenda_items.title: Resolution Regarding 2026 Constitutional Amendments (Tax Caps)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Millicent Rogers and board members present a resolution highlighting the impact of the 2026 constitutional amendments (income tax caps and property tax limits) on Durham County and Durham Public Schools, encouraging voters to oppose both amendments.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 7-0 (Moved by Millicent Rogers, seconded by Miss Burr)

agenda_items.title: Legislative Steering Committee Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Legislative Steering Committee appointments are discussed and voted upon by the board.

agenda_items.title: Policy 3510 (Religious-Based Exemptions) Second Reading and Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Pitman and the policy committee present Policy 3510 (Religious-Based Exemptions from School Programs) for second reading and adoption, incorporating mandatory 1-hour limits, travel time, and compliance updates while planning for re-tiering in January.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 7-0 (Moved by Millicent Rogers, seconded by Mr. Kase)

agenda_items.title: Policy Prioritization and Tiering Recommendations (As Amended)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Pitman and the policy committee present the policy prioritization and tiering recommendations, establishing a structured three-level agenda format (compliance, community suggestions, cross-references) and finalizing 23 prioritized policies for review.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 7-0 (Moved by Miss Rivero, seconded by Millicent Rogers)

votes.item_title: Bonus Plan Approval (October 9 & October 30)
votes.notes: Contingent upon budget amendment one. Approved unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Millicent Rogers moved and Xavier Cason seconded a motion to approve the bonus plan for permanent transportation employees paid bimonthly on October 9, 2026, and group bonuses for employees paid monthly on October 30, 2026, contingent upon budget amendment one. The discussion touched on monthly DPI compliance data file transmissions and fund balance appropriation mechanics for the bonuses. The board voted unanimously (7-0) to approve the motion.

votes.item_title: State Teacher Supplement Framework
votes.notes: Includes Pre-K and EC Pre-K teachers. Approved unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Natalie Bent Kitaif moved and Millicent Rogers seconded a motion to approve the state teacher supplement framework for those qualified to receive it. Board members noted that this is a new, one-time state-funded teacher supplement program initiated by North Carolina to help level the playing field for districts with smaller tax bases, while acknowledging its uncertain long-term sustainability. The motion passed unanimously (7-0).

votes.item_title: Resolution Regarding 2026 Constitutional Amendments (Tax Caps)
votes.notes: Opposes state income and property tax constitutional amendments. Approved unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Millicent Rogers offered a motion, seconded by Gabrielle Rivero, to approve a resolution regarding the impact of the 2026 constitutional amendments on Durham and Durham Public Schools. The resolution expresses opposition to proposed constitutional caps on income and property taxes, noting that constitutional amendments create rigid restrictions that are much harder for future leaders to change than ordinary legislation. The motion passed unanimously (7-0).

votes.item_title: Legislative Steering Committee Appointments (22 Applicants)
votes.discussion_detail: Millicent Rogers moved and Gabrielle Rivero seconded a motion regarding Legislative Steering Committee appointments involving 22 applicants. The discussion surrounding the surrounding agenda items also addressed meeting scheduling options, public comment requirements, and board calendar cadences. The motion passed unanimously (7-0).

votes.item_title: Policy 3510 (Religious-Based Exemptions) Second Reading and Adoption
votes.discussion_detail: Board member Millicent Rogers moved approval of Policy 3510 (Religious-Based Exemptions) for second reading and adoption, which was seconded by Mr. Cason. The discussion included references to community efforts, such as a sign-on letter by Faith for Public Schools urging community faith leaders to commit to maintaining religious lessons outside school hours on weekends. Board member Miss Rivero inquired about the review process scheduled for January, asking what specific factors would be used to evaluate the policy's implementation, such as student participation numbers and potential misuse. In response, it was noted that the policy would be reviewed alongside administrative feedback and sample policies to ensure student safety, protection, and compliance. The motion ultimately passed unanimously (7-0).

votes.item_title: Policy Prioritization and Tiering Recommendations (As Amended)
votes.notes: Amended to remove policy enforcement item; approved unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Gabrielle Rivero moved and Natalie Bent Kitaif seconded a motion on Policy Prioritization and Tiering Recommendations (As Amended). The board engaged in extensive procedural and logistical discussions regarding meeting cadences, public comment mandates, and appropriate notice timelines before voting. The amended motion passed unanimously (7-0).

meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education held its monthly work session on August 13, 2026. The board recognized students, teachers, and employees of the month, received a superintendent update on the start of the traditional school year, and discussed staffing and technology investments. Formal votes were taken to approve an unlimited instructor staffing contract to establish support for Exceptional Children (EC) teacher vacancies and to approve the purchase of modern interactive panel screens for classrooms.

agenda_items.title: Call to Session and Moment of Silence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board convened its monthly work session, welcomed attendees, and held a moment of silence honoring former Hillside High School coach and DPS alumna Sheremy Dillard.

agenda_items.title: August Celebrations and Recognitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board and administration recognized outstanding members of the DPS community, including the August Student of the Month from the School of Creative Studies, International Thespian Festival FESBY award winners from DSA and Jordan High School, and the Teacher and Employee of the Month.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis provided updates on the start of the traditional school calendar, school visits across the district, the Superintendent's Six operating commitments, and the recent visit by NASA astronaut Christina Cook to Little River Elementary.

agenda_items.title: Unlimited Instructor Contract for EC Teacher Vacancies
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The administration presented a recommendation for an unlimited instructor contract with a third-party staffing agency to help fill critical Exceptional Children (EC) teacher vacancies. Board members deliberated extensively on the urgency of filling vacancies versus adherence to board processes and transparency.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 7-0 (Moved by Mr. Tab, seconded by Miss Burr)

agenda_items.title: Interactive Panel Purchase Recommendation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board discussed and evaluated the purchase recommendation for interactive panel screens to replace legacy BrightLink projectors across district classrooms, noting long-term maintenance savings, professional development plans, and hot-swap inventory.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 7-0, contingent upon county commissioner lease authorization (Moved by board member, seconded by Mr. Tab)

agenda_items.title: Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board entertained a motion to move into closed session pursuant to statutory provisions.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 7-0 (Moved by Miss Burr, seconded by Mr. Kasein)

votes.item_title: Unlimited instructor contract for Exceptional Children (EC) teacher vacancies
votes.notes: Approved unanimously following discussion on process and student needs.
votes.discussion_detail: The board discussed an unlimited instructor contract for Exceptional Children (EC) teacher vacancies, which faced some procedural hesitation and concerns from members regarding the rushed nature of the agenda change and lack of advance public notice. Despite these procedural process concerns and a symbolic no vote philosophy discussed by some members emphasizing process, the motion made by Mr. Tabb and seconded by Miss Burr was voted on and passed unanimously 7-0.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Special Called Meeting | 7/21/26
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education held a special called meeting on July 21, 2026, presiding chair Joy Harrell-Goff. The board discussed and approved the 2026-27 salary scales as amended (passing 4-3), approved parking lot asphalt paving at Southwest Elementary School (passing 6-0), and approved the Lions Farm Elementary Learning Village classroom expansion along with referring boundary discussions to the facilities committee (unanimous). Finally, the board voted unanimously to adjourn into closed session.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Welcome & Moment of Silence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board chair opened the special called meeting, welcomed staff, parents, and constituents, noted live Spanish interpretation, and led a moment of silence.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed the agenda, approved moving consent items A and B (Southwest Elementary paving and Lions Farm Elementary expansion) to a new operations section after item 3, and adopted the amended meeting agenda.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed unanimously (7-0), moved by Millicent Rogers, seconded by Mr. Kase

agenda_items.title: 2026-27 DPS Salary Scales Presentation and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the proposed 2026-27 DPS salary scales, incorporating state budget updates, state low-wealth supplements, minimum wage adjustments ($18.22/hr for classified/aftercare staff), and step increases. Extensive debate ensued regarding whether to delay approval or approve immediately to ensure timely July payroll without delaying staff raises.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 4-3, moved by Millicent Rogers, seconded by Mr. Kase (with amendment to bring minimum wage/salary scale discussions to the August 19 finance committee)

agenda_items.title: Southwest Elementary School Parking Lot Asphalt Paving
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board pulled Southwest Elementary School's parking lot asphalt paving project from consent to discuss contractor selection, bidding processes, and completion timelines prior to the start of the school year. Staff explained that Southwest was prioritized among top-need schools based on an asphalt condition database and competitive bidding.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 6-0, moved by Millicent Rogers, seconded by Miss Rivero

agenda_items.title: Lions Farm Elementary Learning Village Classroom Expansion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a proposal for a modular classroom expansion (six modular classrooms and a restroom building) at Lions Farm Elementary School to address severe overcrowding and capacity exceedance. Board members debated community engagement, equity across district facilities, boundary adjustments, and alignment with the district's right-sizing RFP.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed unanimously (7-0), moved by Millicent Rogers, seconded by Miss Burr (with referral to facilities committee)

agenda_items.title: Convene into Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered moving into closed session for personnel and legal matters as stated on the agenda.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed unanimously (7-0), moved by Miss Nate, seconded by Miss Rivero

votes.item_title: Adopt Meeting Agenda as Amended
votes.discussion_detail: The Board considered a motion to adopt the meeting agenda with amendments moved by Millicent Rogers. Specifically, consent agenda line items regarding elementary learning villages and parking lot asphalt paving for Southwest Elementary were moved to a new operations section (section 4, operations A and B) for discussion. The agenda as amended was approved unanimously by a 7-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Approve 2026-27 Salary Scales as Amended
votes.notes: Passed 4-3 (with some members recorded in opposition or abstaining during roll calls/voice votes)
votes.discussion_detail: The Board debated the approval of the 2026-27 DPS salary scales, with discussion focusing on classified staff minimum wages, specifically regarding scale structures and adjustments such as after-school care starting at $18.22. Board member Gabrielle Rivero questioned whether salary scales could be separated or if alternative scheduling/minimum wage discussions could be referred to committee. After clarifying that staff would continue to be paid at previous rates with retroactive pay coming later, a motion was made to approve the salary schedule as amended with the after-school care rate correction and to bring the minimum wage discussion to the August 19th finance committee. The motion passed 4-3, with Gabrielle Rivero voting NAY.

votes.item_title: Southwest Elementary School Parking Lot Asphalt Paving
votes.discussion_detail: The Board discussed the parking lot asphalt paving project at Southwest Elementary School after it was removed from the consent agenda for individual review. Staff explained that the project was selected from a prioritized maintenance database and went through a competitive bidding process involving three separate contractors to ensure completion before the start of the school year. Millicent Rogers moved to approve the Southwest blacktop repair, which was seconded by Gabrielle Rivero. The motion passed by a 6-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Lions Farm Elementary Learning Village Classroom Expansion
votes.discussion_detail: The Board reviewed the Lions Farm Elementary Learning Village classroom expansion project, involving six modular classrooms and a modular restroom building to address ongoing over-capacity issues since the school's opening in 2022. Staff noted that the school is at absolute max capacity in a high-growth area and that boundary adjustments would also need to be explored. Millicent Rogers moved to approve the classroom expansion and refer the boundary and overcrowding discussions to the facilities committee, seconded by Miss Burr. The motion was approved unanimously by a 7-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Convene into Closed Session
votes.discussion_detail: A motion was made by Miss Nate and seconded by Gabrielle Rivero to convene into a closed session for the reasons stated on the meeting agenda. The board voted unanimously (7-0) to approve the motion. Chair announced that the live stream would not resume following the closed session.

disagreements.side_a_position: Immediate approval of modular expansion to address severe overcrowding and safety violations
side_a_arguments: School is severely overcrowded (100+ over capacity), classrooms under stairwells violate fire codes, and 12-15 month lead time requires immediate action for 2027-28
disagreements.side_b_position: Delay or more extensive community engagement and alignment with district right-sizing before committing to modular expansion
side_b_arguments: Concerns regarding community engagement, equity of capital investments across the district, and alignment with the broader right-sizing RFP
disagreements.resolution: Approved unanimously with referral of boundary discussions to the Facilities Committee.
